neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Explains how exponential proliferation and squared-amplitude decay balance in the Hannay-Ozorio rule, relates it to ergodicity, Perron-Frobenius invariance and a dynamical-zeta pole, and transfers the resulting microscopic universality expectation to the zeros.

related_synthesis_entries.title: Universality is generated by long-orbit balance and corrected by arithmetic short structure

section_entries.label: 5. Riemann-Siegel Formulae
section_entries.mathematical_role: Explains stationary truncation, resurgence, high-order divergence and optimal truncation, then transfers the resummation mechanism to pseudo-orbit spectral determinants and complex orbits.

unit_result_entry.why_material: Pairs groups around the half-Heisenberg cutoff so the long tail is approximately the conjugate of the short pseudo-orbit sum, producing a real finite Riemann-Siegel lookalike while exposing exponential term proliferation and remaining discontinuities.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Quantum spectral determinants turn primitive orbits into pseudo-orbit Dirichlet terms
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Builds a real spectral determinant, expands the trace formula into composite pseudo-orbits analogous to integers built from primes, and derives a stationary cutoff at half the Heisenberg time.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Error-function smoothing gives a transferable completion of abrupt resummation
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Replaces the hard cutoff by a complementary-error-function window, improves the attainable zeta accuracy, and transfers the analytic-continuation construction to quantum spectral determinants with reported near-degenerate-level resolution.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Reality reorganizes a divergent long expansion around a stationary half-Heisenberg cutoff: long terms resurge as conjugates of short ones, while late-term divergence dictates optimal truncation and smoothing produces a transferable quantum completion.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The quantum lookalike remains semiclassical, computationally burdened by exponential pseudo-orbit proliferation, and does not supply the unknown Riemann operator.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical compression is the pairing of pseudo-orbits on opposite sides of the stationary period T*: the long-period contribution is recovered approximately as the complex conjugate of the short-period contribution, turning an infinite divergent expansion into a finite real cosine sum.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Analytic continuation in energy relates groups with periods T*+X and T*-X and yields the finite Riemann-Siegel lookalike (5.23), summed over Tn<T*. It can reproduce some low eigenvalues, but in chaotic dimension D>1 the retained pseudo-orbits proliferate exponentially in 1/hbar and the formula jumps when a composite-orbit period crosses T*.
directed.conceptual_reading: Conjugation and reality act as a resummation constraint: the nominally independent long tail is encoded by short data reflected about the half-Heisenberg cutoff. This is genuine structural reuse, but it does not imply computational efficiency because the short side itself can be exponentially large.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are the spectral determinant, composite pseudo-orbits, their periods and actions, the stationary cutoff T*, and conjugate pairing converted into a cosine representation. This transfers the organization of the Riemann-Siegel main sum to semiclassical orbit sums.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The finite representation remains impractical at high energy for D>1, is discontinuous at cutoff-crossing energies, and has no known correction series analogous to the Riemann-Siegel Cr terms. It does not construct a Riemann operator.
directed.uncertainty: The long-short relation and determinant formula are semiclassical and approximate; equation (5.23) is extraction-sensitive. The stated success is limited to some low-lying eigenvalues.

supported: The candidate preserves the approximate conjugate pairing across T*, the finer T*+X/T*-X grouping, the finite cosine lookalike, low-eigenvalue scope, exponential pseudo-orbit burden, cutoff discontinuities, and absence of known Cr-like corrections.
inference: Reading conjugation and reality as a resummation constraint and distinguishing finite representation from computational efficiency are well-anchored conceptual moves.
context_or_ocr_risk: Equation (5.23) is formula-sensitive, but the prose is sufficient for the qualitative long-short and bottleneck claims; exact formula reuse still needs scan verification.
missed_mechanism: The candidate omits the source's second explanation for the efficiency gap: the mean density grows as 1/hbar^D for the chaotic system but only as log t for the quasi-one-dimensional Riemann counterpart.
revision_instructions: Add the contrasting mean-density scaling alongside exponential orbit proliferation as a distinct cause of the high-energy computational bottleneck; otherwise retain the candidate and its approximate/semiclassical qualifications.
